section_summary: This section documents U.S. efforts from 1932 to 1940 to enforce the reciprocal U.S.-Japanese waiver of visa fees and obtain refunds when Japanese consulates charged Americans in error. The principal cases concern missionary W. I. Hilliard, theatrical performer Peter J. Ringens, and Singer Sewing Machine manager Ernest L. Vest and his wife Nan Taylor Vest. The papers include file and cross-reference notes, consular despatches, diplomatic correspondence, internal memoranda, an affidavit, refund vouchers, and Japanese receipts.

subfiles.title: File note for Myers despatch concerning W. I. Hilliard
subfiles.about: Records a report that the Japanese Consulate General at San Francisco charged missionary W. I. Hilliard $10 for a visa despite the reciprocal waiver agreement.
subfiles.summary: The note identifies Despatch No. 482 from Mukden and directs a cross-reference to the visa-waiver file. It characterizes the San Francisco fee charged to Hilliard as a violation of the existing U.S.-Japanese agreement.

subfiles.title: Violation of the reciprocal waiver of visa fees agreement
subfiles.from: M. S. Myers, American Consul General, Mukden
subfiles.about: Reports that W. I. Hilliard was charged $10 by the Japanese Consulate at San Francisco for a non-immigrant visa.
subfiles.summary: Myers encloses Hilliard's June 17 letter and explains that the charge appears contrary to the reciprocal waiver effective July 10, 1926. He identifies Hilliard as an American Seventh-day Adventist missionary in Mukden and gives details of his passport issued at Hankow.

subfiles.title: Hilliard letter reporting the San Francisco visa charge
subfiles.to: M. S. Myers, American Consul General, Mukden
subfiles.about: Notifies Myers that the Japanese Consulate in San Francisco charged Hilliard $10 for a visa on May 5, 1932.
subfiles.summary: Hilliard states that he paid the charge in gold. He believes the fee infringed an agreement between the American and Japanese governments.

subfiles.title: File note for instruction to the Japanese Embassy concerning Hilliard
subfiles.about: Records an instruction concerning the $10 Japanese visa fee charged to W. I. Hilliard for travel through Japan to Manchukuo.
subfiles.summary: The note says the Department called the matter to the Japanese Embassy's attention and enclosed a copy of the visa. It observes that the visa bore no fee stamp or other notation proving payment.

subfiles.title: File note for Singapore Despatch No. 305 concerning Peter J. Ringens
subfiles.about: Records that Peter J. Ringens was charged a Japanese visa fee at Singapore allegedly in violation of the bilateral agreement.
subfiles.summary: The note identifies Ringens as the bearer of a service passport issued at Alexandria on March 27, 1933. It records the charge as S$17.40, equivalent to US$9.75.

subfiles.title: File note for Calcutta Despatch No. 584
subfiles.about: Records an inquiry about Japanese visa fees charged to American missionaries at Calcutta.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Consulate General at Calcutta reportedly charged missionaries Rs. 2/11, approximately $1.01, whether they visited Japan or merely transited it. The despatch requested guidance on whether the waiver agreement permitted fees in missionary cases.

subfiles.title: File note for Osaka Despatch No. 183 concerning Ernest L. Vest
subfiles.about: Records Ernest L. Vest's request for repayment of Japanese visa fees collected in error.
subfiles.summary: The note identifies Osaka Despatch No. 183 and cross-references Vest's individual file. Its subject is the requested refund of improperly collected Japanese visa fees.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference concerning revision of the Japanese-American reciprocal arrangement
subfiles.about: Cross-references Despatch No. 4183 on revision of the reciprocal arrangement and limited-entry certificates for temporary non-immigrant seamen.
subfiles.summary: The sheet points to the original despatch filed under 894.111/84. It links revision of the Japanese-American arrangement with entry-document requirements for non-immigrant aliens temporarily landing while their vessel was in an American port.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference concerning Frances M. Black's visa-fee refund
subfiles.about: Cross-references a refund request for a visa fee paid by Frances M. Black.
subfiles.summary: Black is identified as a teacher at Miyagi Girls' School in Sendai. The sheet directs the reader to Yokohama Despatch No. 675 and her individual file.

subfiles.title: Letter transmitting the Ringens refund
subfiles.from: Wilbur J. Carr, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Transmits a $9.88 draft to Ringens and acknowledges his wish to thank the American Ambassador at Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: The Department encloses the refund draft arising from the previously handled Japanese visa-fee case. It tells Ringens that a copy of his letter of appreciation is being sent to the Ambassador in Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Forwarding Ringens's appreciation to the American Ambassador
subfiles.about: Forwards a copy of Ringens's letter expressing appreciation for the Embassy's work in obtaining his refund.
subfiles.summary: The Department refers to Embassy Despatch No. 1470 of September 16, 1935. It explains that the enclosed letter thanks the Ambassador for his interest in Ringens's behalf.

subfiles.title: Ringens letter of thanks and forwarding address
subfiles.to: Chief, Passport Division, Department of State
subfiles.about: Thanks the Department for arranging the Japanese visa refund and supplies a Miami address for the check.
subfiles.summary: Ringens asks that the refund check be mailed to 330 East Flagler Street, Miami. He also requests that his appreciation be conveyed to the American Ambassador in Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Draft letter requesting Ringens's mailing address
subfiles.about: Advises Ringens that a $9.88 refund has been received and requests the address to which it should be sent.
subfiles.summary: The draft recounts that the Singapore consulate reported the improper collection and that the American Ambassador made representations in Tokyo. It states that the refund draft will be endorsed and forwarded once Ringens provides a current address.

subfiles.title: Whereabouts of Mr. Peter J. Ringens
subfiles.about: Reports information obtained from Tokyo about Ringens's probable return to the United States and his possible Miami address.
subfiles.summary: The Tokyo Consulate General believed Ringens left Japan for the United States in October, based on the visa application of his Swedish assistant, Elis Josef Napoleon Lindstrom. That application gave Ringens's address as 3652 Southwest Second Avenue, Miami, rather than the 3560 address to which the Department's earlier letter had been sent.

subfiles.title: Instruction seeking Peter J. Ringens's whereabouts
subfiles.about: Asks the Singapore consulate to determine whether Ringens's current whereabouts are known.
subfiles.summary: The Department reports that a $9.88 refund had been obtained but that its letter to Ringens at 3560 Southwest Second Street, Miami, was returned unclaimed. It requests assistance in locating him.

subfiles.title: Internal comments sheet for the Ringens refund
subfiles.about: Records an internal handling instruction concerning the Ringens file and the $9.88 refund.
subfiles.summary: The sheet directs attention to Ringens's individual file. A handwritten comment concerns delivery or disposition of the $9.88 refund check.

subfiles.title: Letter notifying Ringens of the $9.88 refund
subfiles.from: John J. Scanlan, Acting Chief, Passport Division
subfiles.about: Notifies Ringens that a $9.88 refund draft has been received and asks where it should be mailed.
subfiles.summary: Scanlan explains that representations by the American Ambassador at Tokyo produced a refund of the fee collected at Singapore. The Department will endorse and forward the draft after Ringens supplies his desired mailing address.

subfiles.title: File copy of letter notifying Ringens of the refund
subfiles.from: John J. Scanlan, Acting Chief, Passport Division
subfiles.about: File copy of the Department's request for Ringens's address so that the $9.88 refund could be forwarded.
subfiles.summary: The copy repeats that the American Ambassador's representations in Tokyo secured repayment of the visa overcharge. It notes a check as an enclosure and bears October 1935 receipt and filing stamps.

subfiles.title: Refundment of visa fee erroneously charged Peter J. Ringens
subfiles.from: Edwin L. Neville, Chargé d'Affaires ad interim, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Forwards a $9.88 draft representing the refund of Ringens's Japanese visa fee.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese Foreign Office sent the Embassy a bill of exchange for ¥34.23, equivalent to the S$17.40 originally collected. After conversion it yielded $9.88, which Neville forwards with copies of the related Japanese letter and the Embassy's acknowledgment.

subfiles.title: Horinouchi letter transmitting the Ringens refund
subfiles.from: Kensuke Horinouchi, Director, Bureau of American Affairs
subfiles.to: Edwin L. Neville, American Chargé d'Affaires
subfiles.about: Transmits a ¥34.23 bill of exchange to refund the visa fee wrongly charged to Ringens.
subfiles.summary: Horinouchi says the Japanese Consul General at Singapore attributed the collection to a misunderstanding by the consulate. The enclosed bill was drawn on the Yokohama Specie Bank and represented S$17.40.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of the Ringens refund
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of the bill of exchange refunding Ringens's visa fee.
subfiles.summary: Neville thanks Horinouchi for transmitting ¥34.23. He states that the money has been forwarded to the Department of State for payment to Ringens.

subfiles.title: Collection of visa fee from Peter J. Ringens
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese action on the request to refund Ringens and clarify the visa waiver for theatrical performers.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy informed the Foreign Office that an equivalent Japanese traveler would not be charged by the United States. Japanese authorities said the Singapore consul would be instructed to refund Ringens if the fee resulted from a misconception and thereafter to exempt American theatrical performers making temporary visits.

subfiles.title: Instruction to Singapore concerning the Ringens representations
subfiles.from: Wilbur J. Carr, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the Singapore report and encloses the Department's instruction to the American Ambassador at Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: The Department restates the S$17.40 fee collected from Ringens on March 9, 1935. It informs the Singapore consulate that the matter has been referred to the Ambassador for representations to the Japanese authorities.

subfiles.title: Instruction to Tokyo to seek the Ringens refund
subfiles.from: Wilbur J. Carr, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Directs the Embassy to request a refund for Ringens and clarification that the waiver applies to theatrical performers.
subfiles.summary: The Department explains that the Singapore consul believed the waiver covered only tourists and business travelers, not performers. It invokes the exchanged notes of July 1926, asks for repayment and corrective instructions, and notes that the United States would not charge a Japanese visitor in equivalent status.

subfiles.title: Reciprocal waiver agreement and the Ringens visa fee
subfiles.about: Reports the Japanese visa fee charged to Ringens and questions whether the waiver covered theatrical performers.
subfiles.summary: Ringens, a high diver performing temporarily in Japan, was charged S$17.40 despite appearing to qualify as a non-immigrant under the Immigration Act of 1924. The Japanese Consul General at Singapore interpreted the agreement as limited to tourists and business travelers, prompting McEnelly to request clarification.

subfiles.title: Letter forwarding the Vest refund
subfiles.from: R. B. Shipley, Chief, Passport Division
subfiles.about: Informs Vest that the Department obtained and enclosed a $20 refund for the visas issued to him and his wife.
subfiles.summary: Shipley refers to Vest's April 22 affidavit about two $10 fees collected by the Japanese Consulate General at San Francisco. He reports that the American mission in Tokyo secured the full refund from the Japanese Government.

subfiles.title: Public voucher for the Vest refund
subfiles.about: Records authorization of a $20 refund for fees paid by Vest.
subfiles.summary: The voucher lists a $20 balance authorized for refund and provides for a Treasury check in the same amount. It serves as the accounting record accompanying the repayment.

subfiles.title: Refund to Mr. and Mrs. Ernest L. Vest
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Forwards the $20 refunded by Japan for visa fees improperly charged to Ernest and Nan Taylor Vest.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy reports that its July 25 note prompted a Japanese investigation which found the fees had been collected in error. Grew encloses the currency for transmission to the Vests, together with copies of the Embassy's note, the Japanese reply, and the acknowledgment.

subfiles.title: Embassy note requesting refunds for the Vests
subfiles.about: Requests investigation and repayment of the two $10 visa fees charged to Ernest and Nan Taylor Vest at San Francisco.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy explains that Vest had lived in Japan since 1922 as a Singer Sewing Machine Company representative and had never previously paid for a Japanese visa. It argues that his commercial residence, and his wife's associated status, fell within the 1926 waiver and the 1911 Treaty of Commerce and Navigation.

subfiles.title: Japanese Foreign Ministry note refunding the Vest fees
subfiles.about: Confirms that the Vests' visa fees were collected in error and encloses $20 for repayment.
subfiles.summary: The Ministry reports that its investigation established an error by the officials concerned. It asks the Embassy to transmit the enclosed American currency to Mr. and Mrs. Vest.

subfiles.title: Embassy acknowledgment of the Vest refund
subfiles.about: Acknowledges receipt of the $20 refunded for the Vests' visas.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy refers to Japanese Note Verbale No. 117 of October 21, 1939. It confirms that the money is being transmitted to Mr. and Mrs. Vest.

subfiles.title: Visa Division memorandum on the Vests' treaty status
subfiles.about: Analyzes the treaty and non-immigrant provisions relevant to the Vests' request for refunds.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum cites Article I of the 1911 Treaty of Commerce and Navigation and consular rules governing treaty-alien classification. It suggests the San Francisco consul may have mistaken the Vests' planned four-year stay for non-temporary residence, but recommends omitting that potentially weakening fact from the initial refund request.

subfiles.title: Instruction No. 1757 to seek refunds for the Vests
subfiles.from: G. S. Messersmith, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.to: Joseph C. Grew, American Ambassador, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Directs the Embassy to ask Japanese authorities to refund the two visa fees charged to Ernest and Nan Taylor Vest.
subfiles.summary: The Department describes Vest's long residence in Japan as a Singer Sewing Machine representative and notes that he had not previously been charged. It concludes that the Vests likely came within the business and treaty-trader categories protected by the waiver and asks the Embassy to report the result of its representations.

subfiles.title: Department reply to the Osaka Consul General concerning Vest
subfiles.from: G. S. Messersmith, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Advises that the Embassy in Tokyo is being asked to seek refunds of the $20 paid by the Vests.
subfiles.summary: The Department acknowledges Osaka Despatch No. 183 and regards the charges as apparently contrary to the visa-waiver agreement effective since 1926. It promises a further communication after receiving the Embassy's reply.

subfiles.title: Request for refund of Japanese visa fees collected from the Vests
subfiles.about: Forwards Ernest L. Vest's affidavit and asks the Department to obtain repayment of two $10 visa fees.
subfiles.summary: The despatch identifies Vest as manager of the Kobe Central Agency of the Singer Sewing Machine Company and argues that he qualified for gratis visas under the 1911 treaty. It notes his history of fee-free travel and supplies the New York address to which any refund should be sent.

subfiles.title: Affidavit of Ernest L. Vest
subfiles.about: Describes the collection of two $10 Japanese visa fees at San Francisco and requests their refund.
subfiles.summary: Vest states that he and Nan Taylor Vest obtained their visas on March 28, 1939, before sailing for Japan, although his earlier visas had been free. He recounts being told that businessmen residing in Japan had to pay, asserts that the commercial treaty exempted him, and attaches the original receipts as evidence.

subfiles.title: Japanese consular receipt issued to Ernest L. Vest
subfiles.about: Receipt for one of the $10 Japanese visa fees paid by Ernest L. Vest.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese-language form records consular receipt of the fee in Shōwa 14. It is one of the two original receipts attached to Vest's affidavit as proof of payment.

subfiles.title: Japanese consular receipt issued to Nan Taylor Vest
subfiles.about: Receipt for the second $10 Japanese visa fee, paid for Nan Taylor Vest's visa.
subfiles.summary: The Japanese-language form is the companion to Ernest Vest's receipt and dates from Shōwa 14. It was attached to the affidavit to substantiate the couple's total payment of $20.
